note: Royal Decree No. 1238 of 14 October 2016 (Lovtidende A, published 15 October 2016), which put the Danish Act on the Processing of Personal Data (Act 429 of 2000) in force for Greenland in the wording it sets out, from 1 December 2016, read in full from retsinformation.dk; Greenland keeps this act, not the Danish Data Protection Act of 2018 that rests on the GDPR. Section 20(3) as it applies in Greenland: credit bureaus may not process information against a person's creditworthiness more than five years old, unless in the individual case it is plainly decisive: written as keep 5, as Denmark's file reads the same rule. Datatilsynet's guide to the act for Greenland (2016, the copy on its site read 2026-10-31) says a credit bureau must get Datatilsynet's permission before it begins and must tell a person within four weeks of registering them; it names no bureau working in Greenland, and none was found, so the bureau is the act's licensed bureaus. No source states how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the bureau's next monthly update. No later decree replacing No. 1238 was found (retsinformation.dk's 2019 decree No. 1325 for Greenland concerns financial legislation only).

sources.title: Lovtidende A 2016 No. 1238: Anordning om ikrafttræden for Grønland af lov om behandling af personoplysninger (14 October 2016)
sources.said: Anordning om ikrafttræden for Grønland af lov om behandling af personoplysninger ... skal gælde for Grønland i følgende affattelse: ... § 20. Kreditoplysningsbureauer må kun behandle oplysninger, som efter deres art er af betydning for bedømmelse af økonomisk soliditet og kreditværdighed. ... Stk. 3. Oplysninger om forhold, der taler imod kreditværdighed, og som er mere end 5 år gamle, må ikke behandles, medmindre det i det enkelte tilfælde er åbenbart, at forholdet er af afgørende betydning for bedømmelsen af den pågældendes økonomiske soliditet og kreditværdighed. ... Anordningen træder i kraft den 1. december 2016.

sources.title: Datatilsynet: Datatilsynets vejledning om persondataloven for Grønland (2016)
sources.said: Et kreditoplysningsbureau skal søge Datatilsynet om tilladelse, før bureauet må begynde sin virksomhed. ... Hvis en person eller en virksomhed bliver optaget i et register hos et kreditoplysningsbureau, skal bureauet give vedkommende besked om dette, inden der er gået fire uger efter registreringen.
